trickyParts: The pod is replaced every two hours or so, and each replacement takes the issue volume with it: both local Postgres clusters, every scratch file and every unpushed commit. Push after each seam. Two pod rolls cost work that the INFRA merge lane rescued to a branch; the third was survived by pushing first.

The measurement Postgres is a Job in the cluster's builds namespace, which a Legion release roll does not replace, so the seeded database outlives this pod. Job infra-325-postgres-w6pft, Service of the same name, image mirror.gcr.io/pgvector/pgvector@sha256:2358fcba361ed2233a5ed81b5fe4ca779ccb304120ce531a3bf51c0ed7e2bc11 (Postgres 18.6), 8 CPU, 32Gi, a 200Gi build-scratch ephemeral volume, activeDeadlineSeconds 43200. Its URL and password are in /legion/scratch/tmp/bench-job.env, which dies with the pod; read the Service and the Job's env to rebuild it. DELETE IT WHEN THE LAST MEASUREMENT IS DONE: kubectl -n builds delete job infra-325-postgres-w6pft, which takes its Service with it.

The local Postgres the Go tests run against is a rootless Postgres 17 unpacked onto the issue volume; /legion/scratch/pg/setup.sh rebuilds it, and 'bash setup.sh bench' builds a second cluster with durability on. A replacement pod re-runs it. For psql by hand, export PATH=/legion/scratch/pg/root/usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin:$PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/legion/scratch/pg/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/legion/scratch/pg/root/usr/lib/postgresql/17/lib around the command.

internal/dispatch/api cannot run in this pod: api/rank_test.go refuses a cluster whose only collation is byte order, and storetest templates every test database from that cluster. Each test of that package runs under -run, and the whole package is CI's to run. The pod runs refs, docs, store, benchtime, explaintest and cmd/dispatch-seed.

A plan assertion that only demands an index condition proves nothing: ask_followers' primary key (ask_id, session_id) gives the session arm a full index scan with a condition on its non-leading column, so the backlink count's plan test passed with its own migration removed. Every index assertion in this change names the index or checks the condition is on the index's first key column, read with pg_get_indexdef(indexrelid, 1, true).

Migration numbers 0150 to 0159 are contiguous after main's 0149. The INFRA merge lane reports that sjawhar/legion#2411 is armed and closes the numbered series at 0149, requiring YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<slug>.up.sql for every new migration; once it is on main this block must be renamed, which is the last forward merge's work. Five open pull requests also claim 0150 upward.
deviations: The migration numbering the plan gave (0153 onward) was impossible: store_test.go's TestMigrationSetIsNumberedOneToN refuses a gap, and main's highest is 0149, so the block starts at 0150.

The plan's protocol 2 says to seed the before side with the branch's seed tool against a schema migrated from main. The seed's last step called this branch's refresh, which reads search_term_totals.snapshot and search_term_queue, so it failed on main's schema and failed the command. The seed now reads the schema from the catalogue and takes the matching build, which is what makes protocol 2 runnable at all.

The five document-arm statements cannot be a protocol 1 pair, so the timing test reads whether document_search exists and measures main's own text where it does not, naming the side in the measurement's label. That makes the two-commit run one test against two databases rather than a second harness.
openQuestions: R2's share-of-plan reading is recorded in the pull request and its answer is a reason, not a fix: after the change searchQueryMeaning's time is in the meaning arms' embedding reads, 627 ms of a 1,623 ms plan (38.7%) in one Index Scan using embeddings_pkey, with 132 ms and 96 ms more on that index in the other two meaning arms, each a primary-key lookup of one 1,536-dimension vector per candidate row. No index is missing and no join replaces a per-candidate key lookup. The next part down is a parallel scan of comments behind a hash left join at 5.4%, below R2's 10% bar.

A9's route timings are not finished, and one defect blocks two of its six cases. Four routes time cleanly against a server booted on the corrected seeded database (a smoke run at five requests gave medians of 21.8 ms for a comment, 101.3 ms for an ask and 22.3 ms for a message). The two upload cases answer 404: an upload over a document THE SEED WROTE is refused, while an upload under a new name answers 201 and a second upload over that same server-written document answers 201 too. The seed's documents are outside the Proof schema the document write path needs — the same reason GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/text answers an empty markdown for them, and the reason cmd/dispatch backfill-block-ids reports 'document is outside the Proof schema; replace the document from markdown to repair it' for every one. The seed writes artifact_versions and the block index but not the ygo document state a version written through the API carries. Until the seed writes that state, A9's two upload cases cannot be driven, and they are the two the new triggers cost most on.

The agents route answers 503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE against this fixture because no Envoy listener runs beside it, not because of this change. agentLastActivity's own statement is measured and its equality test passes; the route needs a fixture with a listener.
discoveredComplexity: Driving the routes against a production-shaped database found two defects no test had: the seed wrote no ask.opened event for any of its 80,000 asks, so every ask read answered 500, and its filler ask.opened events carried a payload that is no ask, so the events route answered 500 too. Both are fixed and both now have a test of the seed that fails without the fix. This is what the boot-and-drive rule is for: the Go suites were green throughout.

The closure's fault was not a missing index. document_blocks_node_id exists; the exists probe sat inside a disjunction, where no semijoin can carry a qual, so Postgres planned it as a hashed subplan that materialised all 800,000 rows, twice. A lateral with limit 1, plus an explicit to_kind in ('artifact','block') so the planner can still derive the target kinds, is what keyed it.
